findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the casing between the SKILL.md principle text and the AC grep (use `grep -ic` or quote the exact landed casing) so a byte-identical transfer satisfies the criterion.
evidence: AC: "checked by `grep -c 'Volume is not a reason to skip a concern'` returning 1"
Approach: "and \"volume is not a reason to skip a concern.\""
Verify-command taxonomy item (1): anchor/substring — case-sensitive grep will not match a differently-cased landed string
findings.finding: The SKILL.md acceptance-criterion greps for capital-'V' `'Volume is not a reason to skip a concern'`, but the Approach section states the principle in lowercase — '"volume is not a reason to skip a concern."'. grep is case-sensitive by default, so a faithful verbatim transfer of the lowercase text would make this AC's `grep -c ... returning 1` fail (return 0).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (SKILL.md bullet) vs Approach (SKILL.md principle text)
scenarios: Executor transfers the authored lowercase 'volume...' text byte-identically, then the AC grep returns 0 and the criterion appears to fail despite a correct transfer.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC to `grep -ic 'volume is not a reason to skip a concern'` (case-insensitive) or match the grep pattern's casing exactly to the authored source text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `do_not_move` artifact in concern (10): its schema/fields, its exact target file (name 'the playbook' concretely, e.g. `.rebar-janitor/tools.md` vs a new file), and the phase/step that consumes it as an edit gate — reconciling it with Discovery's finding-only output schema and the 'Never edit code' principle.
evidence: Plan: 'require each shard's `do_not_move` list to be appended to the playbook before any edit lands'
discovery.md output schema fields are only finding/concern/location/evidence/scenarios/why_it_matters — no `do_not_move`
SKILL.md line 76-78 names `.rebar-janitor/tools.md` as 'the durable playbook'; 'playbook' in concern 10 is otherwise undefined
SKILL.md line 54: 'Never edit code' — Discovery emits findings, not edits, so 'before any edit lands' has no in-phase referent
findings.finding: Concern 10 references a `do_not_move` list that must be 'appended to the playbook before any edit lands', but the plan defines neither the artifact's schema, its target file (the skill elsewhere calls `.rebar-janitor/tools.md` 'the durable playbook'), nor its consumer — and it is introduced in Discovery, a phase whose output schema has no such field and which per the skill's core principle 'Never edit code'.
findings.location: Approach → discovery.md concern (10); phases/discovery.md output schema (lines 87-98)
scenarios: A Discovery subagent sharding concern 10 must emit a `do_not_move` list but has no schema, target file, or consuming step to write it to

verification.md defines only is_verifiable / evidence_entails_finding / impact_follows_necessarily / no_viable_alternative_explanation, the 5 impact attributes, and cited_reference_accurate — no 'remediation-direction' axis
Remediation is Phase 3 (SKILL.md pipeline diagram, lines 27-32); Phase 2 has no remediation-direction concept
findings.finding: The new 'Streaming validation' section directs the verifier to validate 'along three axes at once (correctness, impact validity, remediation-direction validity)', but Phase-2 Verification's defined contract is 4 binary sub-questions + 5 impact attributes + a citation veto; 'remediation-direction validity' is not any of these and remediation is Phase 3, so a referenced decision axis is left without a defined vocabulary or co-located mapping to the scoring machinery.
findings.location: Approach → verification.md 'Streaming validation' section; phases/verification.md (sub-questions lines 20-31, impact attributes 44-56)
